newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to hold to 1997 deficit target - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Germany to hold to 1997 deficit target - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday, after the release of new forecasts showing tax revenues would be lower than expected in 1996 and 1997, that he would hold to his planned budget deficit target next year.
"We will stick to planned new borrowing of 56.5 billion marks in 1997," Waigel said in a statement after the publication of the tax estimates.
The estimates, by an independent working panel, said 1997 total tax revenues would be 10.3 billion marks down on the last forecast in May and 1996 revenues would be five billion marks lower.
Federal revenues are seen down by five billion marks next year after a fall of three billion marks this year.

Waigel, who is determined to make Germany qualify under the strict criteria for European monetary union, said the downward revision in 1997 tax projections had already been covered by savings included in its Programme for More Jobs and Growth.

Further savings of seven billion marks have been included in the 1997 draft budget, but Waigel said he was still seeking cuts of three billion marks in spending next year. A cabinet meeting earlier on Friday reached broad agreement on the cuts, which will be reviewed by the three coalition parties.
